crop_profile.summary: Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) is an annual fruit crop thriving in warm, humid climates with 18-30°C temperatures, 60-80% humidity, and 500-1000 mm annual rainfall. It prefers loam soils, pH 5.5-7.0, good drainage, and high nitrogen. Drip irrigation, balanced NPK (10-10-10) and organic amendments boost yields of 60-90 t/ha. Major producers include China, India, USA, Turkey, and Egypt. Key challenges are late blight, early blight, Fusarium wilt, and pests like fruit worm, whitefly, and aphids. Proper irrigation, fertilization, timely harvest, and refrigerated storage ensure high-quality marketable fruit.

actions: Activate drip irrigation system today; apply 25 mm of water per week (≈3‑4 mm per day) for the next 7‑10 days, adjusting based on soil moisture sensor readings.
Distribute well‑aged compost or organic manure (≈5 t/ha) uniformly across the field within the next week to raise organic carbon levels.
Mulch the beds with straw or biodegradable film after compost incorporation to reduce evaporation and suppress weeds.
Conduct a rapid field scouting walk today to identify any early signs of late‑blight or other diseases; record observations.
Record irrigation volumes, soil moisture (target 20‑30 % volumetric), and weather humidity daily.

Weekly: Perform visual disease scouting on 10 % of plants; log any blight symptoms and intervene immediately.
